title: Analyze memory usage in detail
description: Detailed analysis of the system memory usage: total, available and used RAM, and the split by process.

windowsCommandTemplate.name: Memory Analysis
windowsCommandTemplate.commandPattern:
$os = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem; $totalGB = [Math]::Round($os.TotalVisibleMemorySize/1MB, 2); $freeGB = [Math]::Round($os.FreePhysicalMemory/1MB, 2); $usedGB = $totalGB - $freeGB; $usedPct = [Math]::Round(($usedGB/$totalGB)*100, 2); Write-Host "=== Memory Summary ==="; Write-Host "Total: $totalGB GB"; Write-Host "Used: $usedGB GB ($usedPct%)"; Write-Host "Free: $freeGB GB"; Write-Host "
=== Top 10 Processes by Memory ==="; Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 ProcessName, Id, @{Name='MemoryMB';Expression={[Math]::Round($_.WorkingSet/1MB,2)}} | Format-Table -AutoSize

linuxCommandTemplate.name: free
linuxCommandTemplate.commandPattern:
free -h && echo '
=== Top Memory Processes ===' && ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 11

notes: WorkingSet = physical memory (RAM). PrivateMemorySize = private virtual memory. On Linux, buff/cache is available memory.

windowsExamples.command: systeminfo | findstr /C:"Total Physical Memory" /C:"Available Physical Memory"

fr.title: Analyser l'utilisation mémoire détaillée
fr.description: Analyse détaillée de l'utilisation de la mémoire système: RAM totale, disponible, utilisée, et répartition par processus.
fr.notes: WorkingSet = mémoire physique (RAM). PrivateMemorySize = mémoire virtuelle privée. Sur Linux, buff/cache est de la mémoire disponible.
